content: This medication may interact with other drugs. It is important to maintain a comprehensive list of all products you are using, including prescription medications, over-the-counter drugs, and herbal supplements. Share this list with your doctor and pharmacist to ensure safe and effective treatment. This medication can interfere with certain laboratory tests, such as the Coombs' test or specific urine glucose tests, potentially leading to inaccurate results. Inform your healthcare provider and laboratory personnel that you are taking this medication to avoid misinterpretation of test results. In the event of an overdose, if the individual exhibits severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, immediately call emergency services (911). If the situation is less critical, contact a poison control center without delay. In the United States, you can reach the poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. This medication has been prescribed specifically for your current condition. Do not use it for other conditions unless directed by your healthcare provider. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is close to the time of your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store the tablets at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Avoid storing them in the bathroom. If you are using the suspension form of this medication, keep it refrigerated but do not freeze it. Discard any unused suspension after 14 days. Do not dispose of medications by flushing them down the toilet or pouring them into a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the medication is safe, effective, or appropriate for your specific situation. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information tailored to your health needs. Common side effects of this medication may include diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, or headache. Remember that your doctor has prescribed this medication because they have determined that the benefits to you outweigh the potential risks of side effects. Rarely, this medication may cause a severe intestinal condition due to a bacteria called Clostridioides difficile (C. difficile). This condition can occur during treatment or weeks to months after treatment has stopped. Prolonged or repeated use of this medication may result in oral thrush or a new vaginal yeast infection. Serious allergic reactions to this medication are rare. However, if you experience symptoms such as rash, itching/swelling (especially of the face, tongue, or throat), severe dizziness, or trouble breathing, seek immediate medical attention. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the United States, contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice regarding side effects. Before taking cefpodoxime proxetil, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, to penicillins, or to other cephalosporin antibiotics (e.g., cephalexin), or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other problems. This medication may reduce the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines, such as the typhoid vaccine. Inform your healthcare provider if you are scheduled to receive any vaccinations. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly needed. Discuss the risks and benefits with your doctor. This drug passes into breast milk and may have undesirable effects on a nursing infant. Consult your doctor before breastfeeding. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase your risk for serious side effects. This document does not contain all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Medications that reduce or block stomach acid (e.g., proton pump inhibitors, H2 blockers, antacids) may decrease the absorption of cefpodoxime, reducing its effectiveness. Ask your doctor or pharmacist how to use these medications safely with cefpodoxime. For optimal results, take this antibiotic at evenly spaced intervals. Continue taking it for the full prescribed duration, even if symptoms improve after a few days. Stopping the medication too early may allow bacteria to continue growing, potentially leading to a relapse of the infection.
